diagnosis.what_happened: scaffold_chapter5_triad.py appended footnote definitions as literal text, and academic-orchestrator approved the deliverable without OpenXML validation.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: The defect emerged from an architectural silo: scaffold_chapter5_triad.py lacked integration with existing pack_native_footnotes utilities, bypassing OpenXML creation.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: All Word docx deliverables must compile footnotes as true native OpenXML Word footnotes with 'word/footnotes.xml' and '<w:footnoteReference>', never as plain text paragraphs.
diagnosis.rationale_why: Superficial content audits fail to inspect the internal OpenXML container structure. Validating physical zip contents ensures document integrity and compatibility.

desired_behavior: Mandate automated zip verification in orchestrator gates to physically validate the presence of OpenXML native footnotes (word/footnotes.xml and <w:footnoteReference>) before approving .docx deliverables. Implement mandatory OpenXML footnote injection.
generalization: Word DOCX documents must strictly enforce structural integrity using native OpenXML elements instead of text simulation.
